get.description: Liveness: the process is up. Never touches the database.
Readiness: the API can serve real requests. 503 while the database is down.

post.description: Web: log in and receive the session in an HttpOnly cookie.
Mobile: log in and receive the token, for `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
End this session and clear its cookies.

get.description: Your logged-in devices, most recently used first.

schema.title: Response Sessions Api Auth Sessions Get

delete.description: Log a device out. Revoking the current session also clears its cookies.

get.description: The whole tree, flat, each category with its child and part counts.

schema.title: Response List Categories Api Catalog Categories Get

post.description: A new category, at the root when no parent is named.

patch.description: Rename a category, move it, or both. Renaming it to its own name changes nothing.

delete.description: Deletes the category and its own attribute definitions. Refuses one still in use.

get.description: Every field the category's parts have, inherited ones marked.

post.description: A new field on the category. A key an ancestor already defines is refused.

patch.description: Label, required, options and position. No stored part value is touched.

delete.description: Removes the definition. The values stay, and their parts are flagged on read.

get.description: A page of parts, narrowed by a name substring and by category.

post.description: A new part, with every value validated against its category's resolved schema.

get.description: One part. A part whose values no longer fit is returned, marked for review.

patch.description: Replaces the details and the whole attribute map, so nothing is saved half-valid.

AttributeProblemResponse.title: AttributeProblemResponse
AttributeProblemResponse.description: One attribute of a part that no longer fits its schema (requirement 5.3).

AttributeValueResponse.title: AttributeValueResponse
AttributeValueResponse.description:
One stored value, in the three forms the web needs (requirements 3.9, 3.10).

`value` is the exact stored value, a string for a number because JSON numbers are
doubles in every client we generate and exactness is the whole point. `display` is the
same number in engineering notation, so 4700 reads as `4.7k`, and `unit` labels it.

CategoryNodeResponse.title: CategoryNodeResponse
CategoryNodeResponse.description: A category as the tree shows it, with the counts requirement 1.11 asks for.

CategorySchemaResponse.title: CategorySchemaResponse
CategorySchemaResponse.description: Every field a category's parts have, its ancestors' included (requirement 2.7).

CurrentUserResponse.title: CurrentUserResponse
CurrentUserResponse.description: The account, plus the workspace this session acts in (ADR 0007).

PartPageResponse.title: PartPageResponse
PartPageResponse.description: One window of the list and the cursor the next one starts from (requirement 4.11).

PartResponse.title: PartResponse
PartResponse.description:
One part with its values, and whatever no longer fits its schema (requirement 5.2).

A value stored under a key nothing defines any more is still here, with no unit: it is
listed as a problem, never dropped (design §2.5).

PartSummaryResponse.title: PartSummaryResponse
PartSummaryResponse.description:
A part as the list shows it: no attribute values, because a page of rows must not
resolve one schema per row (requirement 8.2).

SchemaAttributeResponse.title: SchemaAttributeResponse
SchemaAttributeResponse.description: A field of a resolved schema, marked when it comes from a category above this one.

SessionResponse.title: SessionResponse
SessionResponse.description: A logged-in device. `current` marks the one making this request.

UpdateAttributeRequest.title: UpdateAttributeRequest
UpdateAttributeRequest.description: Label, required, options and position. `key` and `kind` are refused (requirement 2.9).

UpdateCategoryRequest.title: UpdateCategoryRequest
UpdateCategoryRequest.description:
A rename, a move, or both. What the body left out is left alone.

`parent_id: null` is a move to the root, which is a different thing from not sending
it, so the handler asks `moves()` rather than reading the value.

UpdatePartRequest.title: UpdatePartRequest
UpdatePartRequest.description:
Replaces the details and the whole attribute map (requirement 4.8).

`category_id` left out keeps the part where it is; sent, it moves the part and the
values are validated against the new category's schema (requirement 4.10).
